A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PASCAL and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and some section and table reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification accuracies, adaptive layerwise quantization experiments, activation statistics, and spike-rate measurements on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, adds ImageNet quantization configurations, and reports original accelerator simulation results for energy consumption and latency in Appendix A.10.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same three-stage conversion procedure, spike accumulation and inhibition, AL metric, clustering, and retraining procedure. The new hardware implementations and revised cost accounting do not establish a change to the proposed conversion algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ILSVRC 2012 ImageNet. The added ImageNet configurations and hardware evaluations reuse this coverage; they introduce settings and measurements rather than new datasets or input scenarios.

E2.justification: The original conversion and early-exit comparators are retained. v2 adds a reported comparison with TET, attributed to Deng et al. (2022), in Table 17, plus default-IF LoAS and SparTen ANN hardware comparisons in Appendix A.10. The revised Hao et al. entries retain the same comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 replaces raw timestep reporting and the simple layer-average Teff with IF-energy-adjusted Tnorm and Teff, assuming a spike rate of 0.75 per layer. It adds INT8 energy estimates, cycle-accurate accelerator evaluation, and two ImageNet AL configurations. The reported Hao et al. comparison settings also change from T=8 to T=16 on CIFAR-100 and T=32 on ImageNet; this does not establish that those baselines were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix A.10 supports the small-overhead argument through analytical estimates for representative layers. v2 substantially extends this investigation with controlled accelerator simulations comparing default and PASC IF neurons, separating IF energy from total energy and quantifying latency. The existing threshold-sensitivity and layerwise spike-rate analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental outcomes. The retained statistical quantities used to construct the AL metric do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 accuracies are unchanged. v2 Table 4 adds ImageNet results of 73.98% at Teff=12.40 for VGG-16 and 75.78% at Teff=12.94 for ResNet-34. Existing timestep values change under the new metric, including 2.41 to 3.14 at unchanged 95.34% accuracy. The Hao comparisons change from 76.52% at T=8 to 76.77% at T=16, and from 74.17% at T=8 to 73.93% at T=32, so these are not same-setting performance changes. INT8 energy estimates, hardware energy and latency results, and TET comparison entries are also added.

T1.justification: The mathematical-equivalence definitions, conversion theorems, and Appendix A.1 proofs are substantively retained. The cost analysis changes: v1 Appendix A.10's IF-to-MatMul overhead formulas are reworked into energy-ratio derivations, a new Tnorm definition, and an energy-weighted Teff in v2 Sections 4.2–4.3.

C1.justification: The abstract reduces the claimed inference-timestep advantage from 64× to 56× while retaining approximately 74% ImageNet accuracy. The central contributions—mathematically equivalent conversion and adaptive layerwise quantization—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 extends the small-overhead interpretation to simulated end-to-end energy and latency, explaining the role of MatMul-dominated computation and LoAS's temporal-parallel dataflow. Appendix A.11 also extends the dataset-complexity advantage argument to direct training. These are localized extensions of the existing efficiency interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability URL and substantial implementation information for the new hardware evaluation: modified LoAS and QCFS-enabled SparTen, INT8 weights, Verilog RTL, Synopsys Design Compiler, 40 nm CMOS, 560 MHz operation, and cycle-accurate simulation. The original optimizer, learning-rate, scheduler, and weight-decay disclosures in Appendix A.8 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yin et al. (2024) on LoAS and positions the hardware implementation relative to LoAS and SparTen. It also gives the already-cited Deng et al. direct-training work an explicit comparative role. The original conversion and early-exit research positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: The QCFS description moves from Section 2.2 to Section 3.1, the energy discussion is reorganized into subsections, and the appendices gain hardware and direct-training discussions. Acknowledgements and local wording corrections are added, while most introductory, methodological, and proof prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column TMLR document, extensively reflowing algorithms, equations, and tables. Energy and AL tables gain columns or rows, and new hardware and TET tables appear. Figure 2 is redrawn with a wider horizontal range, and Figure 4 changes panel arrangement. Figures 1, 3, and 4 retain their plotted results; Tables 5 and 6 exchange order.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the efficiency evidence by explicitly accounting for IF overhead and adding synthesis-based, cycle-accurate validation in Appendix A.10, where v1 relied on operation counts and a representative-layer estimate. Code-access and hardware disclosures improve auditability. The gain is bounded: hardware validation covers VGG-16/CIFAR-10, energy-normalized timesteps remain a proxy for latency, and the new TET comparisons use different architectures or timestep budgets. The core conversion results and proofs remain unchanged.
